Search Spanish News / News / Severe storms trigger orange alerts across Mediterranean Spain 4 mins read Published September 9, 2026, 11:34 AM Severe storms trigger orange alerts across Mediterranean Spain Post by Richard Reid Severe storms trigger orange alerts across Mediterranean Spain © russpain.com Share Facebook X WhatsApp Copy link Reddit Spain’s meteorological agency has issued orange alerts for violent storms in the Mediterranean. Heavy rain, hail, and damaging winds threaten Catalonia, Valencia, Murcia, Almería, and the Balearic Islands. Authorities urge caution. Spain's Mediterranean coast is under orange weather alerts as a strong storm front moves in, bringing flash floods, large hail, and damaging winds. The Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet) has warned that the highest risk is in Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Comunidad Valenciana, Murcia, and Almería. Local authorities are preparing for possible disruptions and damage. According to Aemet bulletins for September 9, 2026, orange-level warnings for rain and thunderstorms cover all the Balearic Islands, Catalonia, Murcia, and the Valencian Community. Residents in these regions woke up to warnings about sudden drops in temperature and the risk of localized flooding. The storm, driven by a sharp cold front, is expected to bring heavy downpours and hailstones large enough to damage cars and property. Strong winds could bring down trees and power lines, with the most dangerous conditions expected in the southeast and the Balearic Islands, especially overnight and into Thursday morning. On the northern coast of Alicante, rainfall could reach up to 60 liters per square meter in 12 hours and 40 liters per square meter in just one hour, with a risk of large hail and strong winds. On the Balearic Islands, wind gusts are forecast to reach up to 90 km/h, and orange alerts for heavy rain and thunderstorms have been extended to the entire archipelago. AEMET Aemet spokesperson Rubén del Campo said the orange alerts are staggered: Catalonia remains under warning until 13:59, the Balearic Islands from midday, Comunidad Valenciana and Murcia from 14:00, and Almería from 16:00. Del Campo urged the public to follow Protección Civil advice and avoid unnecessary travel during the worst of the storms. In Catalonia, Protección Civil has already sent ES-ALERT messages restricting movement and activities in several comarcas, including Alt Penedès, Baix Penedès, Garraf, Baix Llobregat, and Vallès Occidental, and has suspended some urgent social and medical services. Seven autonomous communities are under some form of weather alert. Andalucía faces both orange warnings for storms and yellow for heat, while Aragón is on yellow alert for wind. The Balearic Islands, Catalonia, Murcia, and Comunidad Valenciana all face orange-level threats for rain and storms, with additional yellow warnings for wind and rough seas. In Murcia, despite the storm risk, maximum temperatures could still reach 37°C, showing the mix of heat and instability. RTVE and local weather reports note that the front is causing a sharp drop in temperatures by about 8–12°C across eastern Spain and the Balearics, while the southeast remains unusually hot. As the front passes, temperatures are set to fall by 8 to 12 degrees across much of eastern Spain and the Balearics, except for the far southeast where the heat lingers. Northern winds will pick up in the northeast and over the islands, adding to the risk of dangerous conditions. candidates.document_or_record: Murcia cools off after overnight rain and sudden temperature drop
candidates.relevant_excerpt_or_data: Murcia cools off after overnight rain and sudden temperature drop About Last news Culture Celebrities Politics Weather & Nature Events Interesting Madrid Catalonia Valencia Andalusia Regions Last news Culture Celebrities Politics Weather & Nature Events Interesting facts Madrid Catalonia Valencia Andalusia All locations About What are you looking for? Search Spanish News / News / Murcia cools off after overnight rain and sudden temperature drop 3 mins read Published September 10, 2026, 6:48 AM Murcia cools off after overnight rain and sudden temperature drop Post by Richard Reid Murcia cools off after overnight rain and sudden temperature drop © russpain.com Share Facebook X WhatsApp Copy link Reddit After a brief spell of overnight rain, Murcia wakes to cooler temperatures and clearing skies. The weekend brings stable weather, with no return to the recent heat. Murcia wakes up to a noticeable change in the weather. After a night of light rain—just 0.6 litres per square metre—the air is cooler and the sky clears quickly, leaving only a few clouds by midday. The temperature will top out at 28 degrees, several degrees lower than earlier in the week, with early morning lows around 19 degrees. The main shift is the end of the muggy, stormy stretch that has lingered over the region. According to the Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET), any rain will be limited to the early hours, and while there is still a chance of storms, they are not expected to cause problems. By the afternoon, the rain is gone, replaced by a light breeze from the east and a break from the heat. On September 9, several areas of Murcia were under yellow and orange weather alerts due to heavy rain and storms, with local downpours reaching up to 30 litres per square metre in an hour. AEMET Friday looks calm: temperatures in Murcia will hold steady at 30 degrees for the high and 18 for the low. The light easterly wind continues, and while some clouds may stick around, the risk of rain fades. This pattern holds through the weekend. Saturday brings some cloud cover and a return to highs above 30 degrees, while Sunday is expected to be clearer with little change in temperature. Winds stay gentle and from the east, so anyone planning to be outside can expect steady, mild weather. Nearby cities will see similar conditions. Cartagena will have a mix of clouds and light rain, mostly around midnight, easing off by the afternoon. Temperatures there will be close to Murcia's, with lows of 19 and highs of 29 degrees. Alicante will also see a brief midday shower and stable temperatures, staying in the 19 to 29 degree range. These trends match what has been seen across southeastern Spain, where the worst storms have mostly missed the area, as reported earlier in Barcelona. According to regional reports, the weather warnings primarily affected areas such as Vega del Segura, Campo de Cartagena y Mazarrón, Lorca, and Águilas, not just the city of Murcia. The broader southeast of Spain was under the influence of a convective instability front, with alerts issued across several autonomous communities, including Murcia and the Valencian Community. The AEMET forecast points to a break from severe weather and a return to more typical early summer conditions for Murcia and nearby areas. The quick drop in temperature and clearing skies end the recent unsettled spell, though the light rain and lingering clouds are a reminder that the region's weather can still change quickly. For now, residents get a short pause from extremes, but as always, it's worth keeping an eye on the forecast.
